content.title: About
content.content: Flour, bread, white, enriched, unbleached is a versatile baking ingredient made from selected wheat varieties. Enrichment adds B‑vitamins and iron, while the unbleached process retains the grain’s natural flavor and nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Enriched flour helps fill dietary gaps for vitamins and minerals.
Unbleached flour retains higher protein and mineral levels than bleached varieties.
White flour provides a soft texture ideal for breads and rolls.
Wheat flour is the primary carbohydrate source in most countries worldwide.
Traditional wheat flour is used in over 2,000 recipes.

items.title: Rich source of energy
items.content: Flour supplies complex carbohydrates that provide sustained energy.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Dietary fiber in flour promotes healthy bowel function.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Enrichment adds thiamine, riboflavin, and niacin, essential for metabolism.

items.title: Iron
items.content: Fortified flour helps maintain normal hemoglobin levels.

items.title: Protein
items.content: Flour contains plant‑based protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may develop an allergy or gluten intolerance.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Large portions can cause rapid blood sugar spikes.

items.title: Gluten content
items.content: Not suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Use the flour for baking bread, rolls, cakes, pancakes, and pizza dough. It can be blended with whole‑grain flour to boost nutritional value. When preparing dough, sift the flour to remove lumps.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store flour in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For long‑term storage, keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent mold growth and fat rancidity.
